correctness.rationale: An irreducible degree-two p-fold has span dimension at most p+1 by the degree–codimension bound and is a quadric hypersurface there; every other degree-two cycle is a pair of p-planes, counted with multiplicity. Smooth quadrics exist since p≥1; two general p-planes span more than a (p+1)-plane since n≥p+2. Thus the projective-bundle and symmetric-product images are distinct components and have dimensions D and 2d. The essential polarization: the wedge of the k linear forms defining a complementary probe restricts to a vector in ∧^(K−1)S* = S⊗det S*. Evaluating the universal quadratic gives a section linear in the tautological quadric and in (det S*)². It has no base point: choose a restriction of full rank with kernel any chosen line on which the quadratic is nonzero. Consequently the hyperplane pullback is ξ+2h, and the map has generic degree one by uniqueness of the span. Pushforward in the lines convention gives s_j(Sym²S*) and the base tangent weights b−a give the stated denominators. On the pair component multiplication of Chow forms gives h₁+h₂ on the ordered product; generic degree two and the rectangular tableau count yield the displayed factor and degrees. The dimensions have difference p(2n−3p−3)/2; at equality precisely the two top-dimensional multiplicity-one components contribute, with the tie in the range for odd p at n=3(p+1)/2. value.rationale: The standard Chow degree is a canonical enumerative invariant, and the top-dimensional degree can miss a whole irreducible component in this family. The uniform quadric calculation makes that component's degree available even at parameter values where it would be invisible to the degree of the whole variety; the distinct dimensions and the equal-dimension ties give precise rules for using the component calculations. This is more than recomputing the known conic benchmark or evaluating a single unmotivated case.
